verses.zh: 我看见羔羊揭开七印中第一印的时候，就听见四活物中的一个活物，声音如雷，说：「你来！」
verses.en: I looked on when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying with a thunderous voice,[NOTE:1] “Come!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “saying like a voice [or sound] of thunder.”

The addition of “and see” (καὶ ἴδε or καὶ βλέπε [kai ide or kai blepe]) to “come” (ἔρχου, erchou) in 6:1, 3-5, 7 is a gloss directed to John, i.e., “come and look at the seals and the horsemen!” But the command ἔρχου is better interpreted as directed to each of the horsemen. The shorter reading also has the support of the better witnesses.

verses.zh: 我就观看，见有一匹白马；骑在马上的，拿着弓，并有冠冕赐给他。他便出来，胜了又要胜。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] I looked,[NOTE:2] and here came[NOTE:3] a white horse! The[NOTE:4] one who rode it[NOTE:5] had a bow, and he was given a crown,[NOTE:6] and as a conqueror[NOTE:7] he rode out to conquer.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of hearing the voice summon the first rider.

The reading “and I looked” (καὶ εἶδον, kai eidon) or some slight variation (e.g., ἶδον, idon) has excellent ms support (א A C P 1611) and its omission seems to come through the mss that have already placed “and look” (καὶ ἴδε or καὶ βλέπε [kai ide or kai blepe]) after the verb “come” (ἔρχου, erchou) as mentioned in the text-critical note on 6:1. Thus, for these copyists it was redundant to add “and I looked” again.
The phrase “and here came” expresses the sense of καὶ ἰδού (kai idou).
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

Grk “the one sitting on it.”sn The one who rode it. The identity of the first rider on the white horse has been discussed at great length by interpreters. Several answers are given: (1) A number understand the rider on the white horse to be Christ himself, identifying this horse and rider with the one mentioned in 19:11, where the identification is clear (cf. 19:13, 16). It must be noted, though, that there is little in common between the two riders beyond the white horse. The word for “crown” is different, the armament is different, and the context here is different (conquest vs. retribution), with three other horsemen bringing catastrophe following. (2) Others see the rider on the white horse representing a spirit of military conquest that dominates human history and leads to the catastrophes that follow. (3) Another possibility is that the white horse rider represents the Antichrist, who appears later in Rev 11:7; 13:17, and is similar to Christ in 19:11 in that they both ride a white horse. This interpretation has been discussed at length by M. Rissi, “The Rider on the White Horse: A Study of Revelation 6:1-8, ” Int 18 (1964): 407-18. This interpretation is the most probable one.
See the note on the word crown in Rev 3:11.

The participle νικῶν (nikōn) has been translated as substantival, the subject of the verb ἐξῆλθεν (exēlthen). Otherwise, as an adverbial participle of manner, it is somewhat redundant: “he rode out conquering and to conquer.”

verses.zh: 揭开第二印的时候，我听见第二个活物说：「你来！」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] when the Lamb[NOTE:2] opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Grk “he”; the referent (the Lamb) has been specified in the translation for clarity here and throughout the rest of the chapter.

verses.zh: 就另有一匹马出来，是红的，有权柄给了那骑马的，可以从地上夺去太平，使人彼此相杀；又有一把大刀赐给他。
verses.en: And another horse, fiery red,[NOTE:1] came out, and the one who rode it[NOTE:2] was granted permission[NOTE:3] to take peace from the earth so that people would butcher[NOTE:4] one another, and he was given a huge sword.
notes: L&N 79.31 states, “‘fiery red’ (probably with a tinge of yellow or orange).”
Grk “the one sitting on it.”
The word “permission” is implied; Grk “it was given to him to take peace from the earth.”

BDAG 979 s.v. σφάζω states, “Of the killing of a person by violence…σφάζειν τινά butcher or murder someone (4 Km 10:7; Jer 52:10; Manetho: 609 fgm. 8, 76 Jac. [in Jos., C. Ap. 1, 76]; Demetr.[?]: 722 fgm. 7; Ar. 10, 9) 1J 3:12; Rv 6:4. Pass. (Hdt. 5, 5) 5:9; 6:9; 18:24.”

verses.zh: 揭开第三印的时候，我听见第三个活物说：「你来！」我就观看，见有一匹黑马；骑在马上的，手里拿着天平。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] when the Lamb opened the third seal I heard the third living creature saying, “Come!” So[NOTE:2] I looked,[NOTE:3] and here came[NOTE:4] a black horse! The[NOTE:5] one who rode it[NOTE:6] had a balance scale[NOTE:7] in his hand.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the summons by the third creature.

The reading “and I looked” (καὶ εἶδον, kai eidon) or some slight variation (e.g., ἶδον, idon) has excellent ms support (א A C P 1611) and its omission seems to have come through the mss that have already placed “and look” (καὶ ἴδε or καὶ βλέπε [kai ide or kai blepe]) after the verb “come” (ἔρχου, erchou) in 6:1. Thus, for these copyists it was redundant to add “and I looked” again.
The phrase “and here came” expresses the sense of καὶ ἰδού (kai idou).
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “the one sitting on it.”
A balance scale would have been a rod held by a rope in the middle with pans attached to both ends for measuring.

verses.zh: 我听见在四活物中似乎有声音说：「一钱银子买一升麦子，一钱银子买三升大麦；油和酒不可糟蹋。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I heard something like a voice from among the four living creatures saying, “A quart[NOTE:2] of wheat will cost a day’s pay,[NOTE:3] and three quarts of barley will cost a day’s pay. But[NOTE:4] do not damage the olive oil and the wine!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
BDAG 1086 s.v. χοῖνιξ states, “a dry measure, oft. used for grain, approximately equivalent to one quart or one liter, quart. A χ.of grain was a daily ration for one pers.…Rv 6:6ab.”

Grk “a quart of wheat for a denarius.” A denarius was one day’s pay for an average worker. The words “will cost” are used to indicate the genitive of price or value; otherwise the English reader could understand the phrase to mean “a quart of wheat to be given as a day’s pay.”
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 揭开第四印的时候，我听见第四个活物说：「你来！」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] when the Lamb opened the fourth seal I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, “Come!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

verses.zh: 我就观看，见有一匹灰色马；骑在马上的，名字叫作死，阴府也随着他；有权柄赐给他们，可以用刀剑、饥荒、瘟疫（或译：死亡）、野兽，杀害地上四分之一的人。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] I looked[NOTE:2] and here came[NOTE:3] a pale green[NOTE:4] horse! The[NOTE:5] name of the one who rode it[NOTE:6] was Death, and Hades followed right behind.[NOTE:7] They[NOTE:8] were given authority over a fourth of the earth, to kill its population with the sword,[NOTE:9] famine, and disease,[NOTE:10] and by the wild animals of the earth.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the summons by the fourth creature.

The reading “and I looked” (καὶ εἶδον, kai eidon) or some slight variation (e.g., ἶδον, idon) has excellent ms support (א A C P 1611) and its omission seems to have come through the mss that have already placed “and look” (καὶ ἴδε or καὶ βλέπε [kai ide or kai blepe]) after the verb “come” (ἔρχου, erchou) in 6:1. Thus, for these copyists it was redundant to add “and I looked” again.
The phrase “and here came” expresses the sense of καὶ ἰδού (kai idou).

A sickly pallor, when referring to persons, or the green color of plants. BDAG 1085 s.v. χλωρός 2 states, “pale, greenish gray…as the color of a pers. in sickness contrasted with appearance in health…so the horse ridden by Death…ἵππος χλωρός Rv 6:8.” Because the color of the horse is symbolic, “pale green” is used in the translation. Cf. NIV, NCV “pale”; NASB “ashen.”
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “the one sitting on it.”
Grk “And Hades was following with him.” The Greek expression μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ (met’ autou, “with him”) is Semitic and indicates close proximity. The translation “followed right behind” reflects this.

Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “with death.” θάνατος (thanatos) can in particular contexts refer to a manner of death, specifically a contagious disease (see BDAG 443 s.v. 3; L&N 23.158).

verses.zh: 揭开第五印的时候，我看见在祭坛底下，有为　神的道、并为作见证被杀之人的灵魂，
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been violently killed[NOTE:2] because of the word of God and because of the testimony they had given.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the introduction of a new and somewhat different topic after the introduction of the four riders.
Or “murdered.” See the note on the word “butcher” in 6:4.

verses.zh: 大声喊着说：「圣洁真实的主啊，你不审判住在地上的人，给我们伸流血的冤，要等到几时呢？」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] cried out with a loud voice,[NOTE:2] “How long,[NOTE:3] Sovereign Master,[NOTE:4] holy and true, before you judge those who live on the earth and avenge our blood?”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “voice, saying”; the participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated here.
The expression ἕως πότε (eōs pote) was translated “how long.” Cf. BDAG 423 s.v. ἕως 1.b.γ.
The Greek term here is δεσπότης (despotēs; see L&N 37.63).

verses.zh: 于是有白衣赐给他们各人；又有话对他们说，还要安息片时，等着一同作仆人的和他们的弟兄也像他们被杀，满足了数目。
verses.en: Each[NOTE:1] of them was given a long white robe, and they were told to rest for a little longer, until the full number was reached[NOTE:2] of both their fellow servants[NOTE:3] and their brothers who were going to be killed just as they had been.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “until they had been completed.” The idea of a certain “number” of people is implied by the subject of πληρωθῶσιν (plērōthōsin).
Though σύνδουλος (sundoulos) has been translated “fellow servant,” the word does not bear the connotation of a free individual serving another. See the note on the word “servants” in 1:1.

verses.zh: 揭开第六印的时候，我又看见地大震动，日头变黑像毛布，满月变红像血，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I looked when the Lamb opened the sixth seal, and a huge[NOTE:2] earthquake took place; the sun became as black as sackcloth made of hair,[NOTE:3] and the full moon became blood red;[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Or “powerful”; Grk “a great.”
Or “like hairy sackcloth” (L&N 8.13).
Grk “like blood,” understanding αἷμα (aima) as a blood-red color rather than actual blood (L&N 8.64).

verses.zh: 天上的星辰坠落于地，如同无花果树被大风摇动，落下未熟的果子一样。
verses.en: and the stars in the sky[NOTE:1] fell to the earth like a fig tree dropping[NOTE:2] its unripe figs[NOTE:3] when shaken by a fierce[NOTE:4] wind.
notes: Or “in heaven” (the same Greek word means both “heaven” and “sky”). The genitive τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (tou ouranou) is taken as a genitive of place.
Grk “throws [off]”; the indicative verb has been translated as a participle due to English style.

L&N 3.37 states, “a fig produced late in the summer season (and often falling off before it ripens)—‘late fig.’ ὡς συκὴ βάλλει τοὺς ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς ὑπὸ ἀνέμου μεγάλου σειομένη ‘as the fig tree sheds its late figs when shaken by a great wind’ Re 6:13. In the only context in which ὄλυνθος occurs in the NT (Re 6:13), one may employ an expression such as ‘unripe fig’ or ‘fig which ripens late.’”
Grk “great wind.”

verses.zh: 天就挪移，好像书卷被卷起来；山岭海岛都被挪移离开本位。
verses.en: The sky[NOTE:1] was split apart[NOTE:2] like a scroll being rolled up,[NOTE:3] and every mountain and island was moved from its place.
notes: Or “The heavens were.” The Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) can mean either “heaven” or “sky.”

BDAG 125 s.v. ἀποχωρίζω states, “ὁ οὐρανὸς ἀπεχωρίσθη the sky was split Rv 6:14.” Although L&N 79.120 gives the meaning “the sky disappeared like a rolled-up scroll” here, a scroll that is rolled up does not “disappear,” and such a translation could be difficult for modern readers to understand.
On this term BDAG 317 s.v. ἑλίσσω states, “ὡς βιβλίον ἑλισσόμενον like a scroll that is rolled up…Rv 6:14.”

verses.zh: 地上的君王、臣宰、将军、富户、壮士，和一切为奴的、自主的，都藏在山洞和岩石穴里，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the kings of the earth, the[NOTE:2] very important people, the generals,[NOTE:3] the rich, the powerful, and everyone, slave[NOTE:4] and free, hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

Here καί (kai) has not been translated; nor is it translated before each of the following categories, since English normally uses a coordinating conjunction only between the last two elements in a series of three or more.
Grk “chiliarchs.” A chiliarch was normally a military officer commanding a thousand soldiers, but here probably used of higher-ranking commanders like generals (see L&N 55.15; cf. Rev 6:15).
See the note on the word “servants” in 1:1.

verses.zh: 向山和岩石说：「倒在我们身上吧！把我们藏起来，躲避坐宝座者的面目和羔羊的忿怒；
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] said to the mountains and to the rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of the one who is seated on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb,[NOTE:2]
notes: Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

It is difficult to say where this quotation ends. The translation ends it after “withstand it” at the end of v. 17, but it is possible that it should end here, after “Lamb” at the end of v. 16. If it ends after “Lamb,” v. 17 is a parenthetical explanation by the author.

verses.zh: 因为他们忿怒的大日到了，谁能站得住呢？」
verses.en: because the great day of their[NOTE:1] wrath has come, and who is able to withstand it?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Most mss (A M bo) change the pronoun “their” to “his” (αὐτοῦ, autou) in order to bring the text in line with the mention of the one seated on the throne in the immediately preceding verse, and to remove the ambiguity about whose wrath is in view here. The reading αὐτῶν (autōn, “their”) is well supported by א C 1611 1854 2053 2329 2344 latt sy. On both internal and external grounds, it should be regarded as autographic.
The translation “to withstand (it)” for ἵστημι (histēmi) is based on the imagery of holding one’s ground in a military campaign or an attack (BDAG 482 s.v. B.4).
